newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 4.6 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 4.6 pct in April.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate dropped to 4.6 percent in April from 5.3 percent in March, the state Employment Security Commission said Tuesday.

"We have not seen a rate this low for South Carolina since June 1990," said Joel Cassidy, executive director of the commission. "Moreover, the state's unemployment rate has dropped almost a full percentage point over the past two months."
Total nonfarm employment grew by 13,700 despite the loss of 1,400 manufacturing jobs, Cassidy said. Most of the losses were in textiles and apparel.
He predicted the state would continue to see low unemployment rates, making it easier for students to find summer jobs this year.
Williamsburg County had the state's highest unemployment rate for April, 13.5 percent, and Beaufort County had the lowest, 1.8 percent.
